title: STATUS OF VAN DHAN VIKAS KENDRA CLUSTERS
body_text:
The Union Minister of Tribal Affairs Shri Jual Oram today laid a statement on the Table of the House that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides financial support for establishment of Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) through Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India Limited (TRIFED) under the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) and Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN). As on date 4,712 VDVKs, covering 12.94 lakh beneficiaries, have been sanctioned in 28 States/UTs, with a total sanctioned amount of Rs. 642.19 crore under both the schemes out of which 3,406 VDVKs are operational. A maximum amount of Rs 15.00 lakhs is provided to State Governments to set up one VDVK for incurring the expenditure on raw material, training and capacity building, tool kits and machinery, mentoring charges, packaging and branding, transportation, storage etc. Revolving working capital is not provided to VDVKs under the schemes.
However, under the Minimum Support Price (MSP) component of the scheme, revolving fund is provided to State Implementing Agencies (SIAs) for undertaking Minor Forest Produce (MFP) procurement from tribal MFP gatherers at MSP, in case the market price falls below the MSP. During the Financial Year 2025–26, an amount of Rs. 2.50 crore has been released to the State Implementing Agency (SIA) of Meghalaya for the procurement of MFP.
Fund release for establishment of VDVKs is undertaken through Treasury Single Account (TSA) system introduced by Ministry of Finance. TSA accounts have been opened by almost all State Implementing Agencies, and funds are being transferred to the TSA accounts of the SIAs. TSA system provides the treasury and central bank total oversight over liquidity, eliminates idle cash parked in commercial banks, and ensures "just-in-time" release of funds for public expenditures. As mentioned in reply to part (a) above, revolving working capital is not provided to VDVKs under PMJVM / PM-JANMAN schemes.
Operational VDVKs are encouraged to graduate into Van Dhan Producer Enterprises (VDPEs) for value addition, aggregation and market linkage based on their performance. One VDPE proposal from the State of Madhya Pradesh has been approved in principle for implementation.
A total of 148 VDVKs are operational in the state of Chhattisgarh under the PM-JANMAN and PMJVM Schemes. Revolving funds amounting to ₹153.66 crores have been released to Chhattisgarh SIA for procurement of MFPs since 2013-14 through which MFPs worth ₹467 crores have been procured by the State till 2025-26. Chhattisgarh SIA has submitted the claim for reimbursement of losses under the MSP operations which is under examination. No proposal for procurement of MFPs has been received from the State of Chhattisgarh during the current financial year.
The matter has been discussed with the SIAs, and they have been advised to devise appropriate mechanisms for transferring funds directly to the bank accounts of VDVKs and ground-level primary procurement agencies. In some States, funds are already being transferred directly to the bank accounts of VDVKs.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs informed Parliament that 4,712 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs), covering 12.94 lakh beneficiaries, have been sanctioned across 28 States/UTs with Rs. 642.19 crore under PMJVM and PM-JANMAN, of which 3,406 are operational. It detailed fund flow mechanisms including the Treasury Single Account system, MSP-based revolving funds for Minor Forest Produce procurement (with Rs. 2.50 crore released to Meghalaya in FY2025-26), and Chhattisgarh's cumulative Rs. 153.66 crore revolving fund since 2013-14 procuring MFPs worth Rs. 467 crore.
enrichment.context:
Van Dhan Vikas Kendras are a flagship initiative under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs aimed at value addition, branding and marketing of Minor Forest Produce (MFP) collected by tribal gatherers, thereby enhancing their livelihoods without requiring migration. The scheme is implemented via TRIFED under the Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana, now subsumed into the broader Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM), and more recently linked to PM-JANMAN, launched to address development gaps among Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs). MSP for MFP is a separate but related mechanism ensuring tribal gatherers receive a minimum guaranteed price for specified forest produce, cushioning them against market price crashes, with State Implementing Agencies (like TRIFED-designated bodies) undertaking procurement using revolving funds.

The move toward VDVKs graduating into Van Dhan Producer Enterprises (VDPEs) reflects a policy shift from basic collection centres toward formal producer companies capable of aggregation, processing and market linkages, similar to Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) in agriculture. The adoption of the Treasury Single Account (TSA) system for fund transfers is part of a wider public financial management reform pushed by the Ministry of Finance to ensure just-in-time release of funds, reduce idle cash with implementing agencies, and improve fiscal transparency—relevant to broader public expenditure governance reforms across centrally sponsored schemes.

prelims_questions.question: The Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) are implemented under which of the following schemes?
options: Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) and PM-JANMAN
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, VDVKs are established with financial support through TRIFED under PMJVM and PM-JANMAN.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Treasury Single Account (TSA) system, as mentioned in the context of Van Dhan Vikas Kendras, is correct?
options: It provides revolving working capital directly to VDVKs
It eliminates idle cash parked in commercial banks and ensures just-in-time release of funds
It is a mechanism exclusively for state government pensions
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states TSA gives treasury and central bank oversight over liquidity, eliminates idle cash in commercial banks, and ensures just-in-time fund release; it does not provide revolving working capital to VDVKs.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of Van Dhan Vikas Kendras in promoting tribal livelihoods through Minor Forest Produce value addition. What are the challenges in their operationalization and graduation into Van Dhan Producer Enterprises?
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Governance: Welfare schemes for vulnerable sections

mains_questions.question: Examine the role of the Minimum Support Price mechanism for Minor Forest Produce in safeguarding tribal gatherers' incomes. How does the Treasury Single Account system improve fund utilization in centrally sponsored schemes?
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 3 - Economy: Public Financial Management and Agricultural Marketing
